paragraphs: Mom has a calendar app on her phone. She puts everything for the month in it. On Sunday night, she shows us the page for November. The first day of the month is a Sunday. On Tuesday, the third of November, I have a school photo. On Saturday, the seventh, Tom has a football game. He plays in goal. He plays well, but he sometimes drops the ball. Dad takes him to the field at three o'clock.

On Sunday, the eighth, we go to Grandma's house for lunch. On Wednesday, the eleventh, my class has a party at school. The second Saturday of the month is the fourteenth. It rains a lot on that day. Tom could not play, because the field is wet. Mom moves the game in her app. Now the game is on Sunday, the fifteenth. Tom looks at the new day and smiles. Pip is happy, too. On Monday, the sixteenth, Pip has a bath.

The third Saturday is the twenty-first. Tom has the school fun run that day. On Sunday, the twenty-second, it is Grandpa's birthday. That week is busy. The weekend is the busiest of the month. The last Saturday is the twenty-eighth. Grandpa takes Tom and me to fish that day. November has more Sundays than Saturdays. Do you know why? The month starts on a Sunday and ends on a Monday. The last day is Monday, the thirtieth.
text.summary: Lily reads the family calendar for November on Mom's phone. Each event has a day and a date, and one game moves to a new day.
